existing_train64_coverage.scope: train64 ontology-class coverage diagnostic only; no heldout/originaldev read, no predictions or public Score, no method/threshold selection
limitations: Coverage ignores extraction, confidence, negation and normalization accuracy; not attainable-score estimate.
Canonical diagnostic is semantic class coverage; publicv2 evaluator does not canonicalize all alt IDs.
Only positive linked mentions tested; model None does not represent correct NIL text output.

findings: Upstream BERT_training constructs a fresh model and compiles/fits without first loading the public H5; using it unchanged is not public-checkpoint adaptation.

Existing strict native loader constructs from_config and overwrites all native variables with exact H5 datasets. Explicit load-before-train is feasible but no training step on these public weights has been tested here.
Native input is lowercased phrase-only maxlen32 CLS and 17266-way softmax. A target supervision contract must handle equivalent original columns, compounds, unseen current HPO and NIL separately.

Old adaptation was final100 self-trained Biomed/2026-head weights, fresh PyTorch Adam, 3 epochs, 1749 positives repeated16 with original HPO/None replay. NO and unlinked spans were excluded from added positives.
Existing training64 coverage is an old coarse class-coverage diagnostic; startswithHP and alias mapping do not prove strict valid-HPO eligibility or per-fold sample counts.
Dictionary generation is outside the neural graph; scores can affect later collision handling, but neural adaptation does not directly teach a dictionary rejection rule.

Fixed LGB features/calibration were learned from original public weights. New NN scores introduce distribution shift; any later control must explicitly freeze or rebuild fold-matched selector ancestry.
